text:
Matias Maccelli has found a home on Long Island, at least for now. After a season in Toronto, he has 11 points in 13 games with the Islanders, 0.85 a game after 0.55 last season, and he has gone from being on the ice for 31% of his team's power-play chances to 77%. That role change is real. Whether the scoring holds is less certain: the Islanders have scored about 4.6 more goals than their chances with him on the ice, which flatters his line.

The skill is real too. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him in the 92nd percentile among forwards for primary shot assists, and 20% of his setups go across the royal road, the pass that moves a goalie side to side, against 7% for a typical forward. NHL.com's Stefen Rosner called one feed to Simon Holmstrom "great sauce." He is a setup man playing with finishers like Holmstrom and Bo Horvat. Thirteen games is a small sample; watch whether he keeps the power-play spot once the lineup is healthy.
